clinician.final_diagnosis: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome Associated with Varicella-Zoster Virus Encephalitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 8-year-old previously healthy boy, vaccinated for varicella at 12 months with no prior chickenpox, presented with 3-day fever, progressive left ear pain/swelling, and vesicular rash around the left ear pinna. Physical examination revealed left ear swelling with erythema extending to pre/post-auricular areas, vesicular lesions with red base on the outer ear canal extending to the left maxillary dermatome, yellowish discharge, and tender left cervical lymphadenopathy (2×3 cm). On day 2 of admission, he developed lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy, establishing Ramsay Hunt Syndrome. On day 3, he developed neurological symptoms consistent with encephalitis (vomiting, dysarthria, unsteady gait) without seizures or meningeal signs. Brain MRI and MRV were normal. CSF analysis showed mild pleocytosis (10 leukocytes: 8 mononuclear, 2 polymorphonuclear) with normal protein and glucose. VZV PCR from ear swab was positive, while bacterial culture and HSV PCR were negative. He was treated with 10 days of IV acyclovir and 7 days of prednisolone (1 mg/kg/day), with significant clinical improvement and asymptomatic discharge.
